title: Strings with NEL, LS, PS and a byte order mark
notes: YAML 1.2 reads these four characters as ordinary text, but YAML 1.1 reads NEL, LS and PS as line breaks, and a byte order mark is a stream marker rather than text. The family writes them as escapes in a double-quoted scalar, so every reader keeps them. This is a writing convention of the family, not the specification: a string is written plain only when every common reader reads it as that same string, so the text is judged under the YAML 1.2 Core schema (loose) and also under YAML 1.1 and the number forms common readers accept (strict).
